answer: A notarized affidavit makes each extra identity pay $15, the California per-signature fee; a farm running N fakes pays N×$15 and cannot share it because each signer must appear in person with ID and leave a thumbprint in a bound journal. A farm reusing one journal entry dies by journal check at 2: the duplicate voids both filings. Each affidavit crosses the canyon archive, climbs the trellis of stamped forms, and rests on the ridge of the recorder's desk. A 500-seat farm needs 500 people in the room and $7,500 before one fake earns.
